Description: Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. The spread of this fatal disease increases in crisis-affected populations. The ongoing Syrian civil war has led to significant damage to the national healthcare system and forced millions of Syrians to take refuge in neighboring countries, where the majority face miserable conditions. These circumstances increase the risk of TB development and spreading among Syrian refugees (SRs) and their host communities. After the beginning of the Syrian crisis in 2011, a remarkable increase in TB cases was reported in countries bordering Syria and is essentially attributed to the massive displacement of the SR population. Here, we first review the risk of TB dissemination during wars and among displaced populations, notably refugees. Then, we discuss the causes, current situation, and complications of the growing TB risk among SRs in Syria’s neighboring countries, focusing in particular on Lebanon. The aim is to highlight the spreading potential of this disease among vulnerable populations facing such complex conditions of conflicts and forced displacements.

Description: A numerical analysis based on 161 phenotypic characteristics was performed with 58 strains of fluorescent pseudomonads isolated from 3 Lebanese spring waters, and 49 type or collection strains belonging or related to genus Pseudomonas. Clusters I, III to V, and VIII were further divided into 14 subclusters. Title: CD3 bright γδ T cells are the major innate source of Interleukin-17A during pneumococcal infection in mice
Authors: Maya Hassane, Bachar Ismail, Fouad Dabboussi, François Trottein, Christophe Paget
Description: Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) is a pro-inflammatory cytokine that plays important roles in a wide range of immune responses including infection as it participates in containment and elimination of microbes. Surprisingly, little is known about the precise functions and the sources of IL-17A during pneumococcal infection. γδ T cells are recognized as major secretors of IL-17A, but more recently the CD3 bright γδ T cell subset has been proved to be more specialized in producing this cytokine than the rest of the γδ T cell population. Here, we demonstrated that γδ T cells, especially the CD3 bright subset, produced massive amounts of IL-17A during the early course of pneumococcal infection. Interestingly, IL-1β and IL-23 were sufficient for IL-17A production by CD3 bright γδ T cells in vitro.
